column1: # Cards the corpus rule excludes and this repo implements anyway.
# `baylee-catalog corpus` decides what gets a `CardIndex` from Scryfall's own
# vocabulary — set type, layout, and Vintage legality inside a joke set. That
# rule is right about Magic and blind to this repo: a card somebody sat down
# and wrote a `CardDef` for needs an index whatever Scryfall says about it,
# because codegen cannot build a card that has no row in the ledger.
# So this is the hand-kept, additive half, like `data/land-cycles.tsv`: every
# line names a card the rule drops and says why it stays. Adding one here and
# rerunning `baylee-catalog corpus` is the documented answer when
# `cargo xtask ledger` reports a card with no row. Removing a line is only
# safe while the ledger has no row for that card yet — an assignment is frozen,
# so a card that has one keeps it whether or not this file still names it.
# A kept card is admitted whole: its row is the corpus query's own, so its
# first-printing set and its place in the order are decided by the same rule
# as every other card's.
# The eight below are all silver-bordered lands — `set_type = 'funny'` with
# `vintage = 'not_legal'`, which is what the joke-set clause drops. They were
# implemented before that rule existed and no acceptance deck plays one.
